Run SQL queries on an in-memory DuckDB d: Starten Sie SQL-Abfragen auf einer DuckDB-Datenbank.
Create DB from data and run query: DB aus Daten erstellen und Abfrage ausführen
Load JSON rows as tables in a temporary: Load JSON rows as tables in a temporary in-memory DuckDB and run one SQL query over them.
Detect the columns and DuckDB types of a: Detect the columns and DuckDB types of a JSON array of rows.
Per-column statistics (min, max, distinc: Per-column statistics (min, max, distinct count, average, quartiles, null %) for a JSON array of rows.
Diff two JSON arrays of rows by key colu: Diff two JSON arrays of rows by key columns into added, removed and changed rows.
Remove duplicate rows from a JSON array,: Remove duplicate rows from a JSON array, matching on key columns or on the whole row.
\n **DO NOT** insert dynamic input: **HINWEIS** Fügen Sie dynamische Eingaben direkt in den Abfrage-String ein. Verwenden Sie stattdessen $1, $2, $3 und fügen Sie sie in Args für parametrierte Abfragen hinzu, um **SQL-Injektion zu verhindern.**
List of tables to create in the database: Liste der Tabellen, die in der Datenbank erstellt werden sollen
Please use $1, $2, etc. for parameterize: Bitte verwenden Sie $1, $2 etc. für parametrierte Abfragen, um SQL-Einschleusung zu vermeiden.
Arguments to be used in the query: Argumente, die in der Abfrage verwendet werden sollen
A JSON object mapping each table name to: A JSON object mapping each table name to its rows, e.g. {"orders": [{"id": 1, "total": 9.5}], "customers": [{"id": 1, "name": "Ann"}]}. Columns come from the row keys and types are detected from the values; a nested object stays one STRUCT column, queried with dot notation (meta.city). Each table needs at least one row.
One DuckDB SQL statement over the tables: One DuckDB SQL statement over the tables above, e.g. SELECT c.name, sum(o.total) AS spent FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY ALL. Quote table or column names that are not plain identifiers with double quotes.
A JSON array of values bound to $1, $2,: A JSON array of values bound to $1, $2, … in the query, in order, e.g. ["IN", 10, null]. Strings, numbers, booleans or null.
A JSON array of row objects, e.g. [{\"id: A JSON array of row objects, e.g. [{"id": 1, "email": "a@b.co"}]. At least one row.
A JSON array of row objects, e.g. [{"id": 1, "amount": 12.5}]. At least one row.
The older dataset: a JSON array of row o: The older dataset: a JSON array of row objects. May be empty.
The newer dataset: a JSON array of row o: The newer dataset: a JSON array of row objects. May be empty.
Column names that identify a row on both: Column names that identify a row on both sides, e.g. ["id"] or ["order_id", "line"]. Values must be unique within each side.
A JSON array of row objects. May be empt: A JSON array of row objects. May be empty.
Column names that identify a duplicate,: Column names that identify a duplicate, e.g. ["email"]. Leave empty to treat only fully identical rows as duplicates.
Which occurrence of each duplicate group: Which occurrence of each duplicate group to keep, by position in rows. Defaults to first.
